[18/12/25, 09:15:10] Yash Gaba Gim Sarc: On Dec 5th, Goa Institute of Management hosted a deeply engaging alumni webinar on “My Academic Journey: Teaching and Learning” for those curious about moving from industry to the classroom.

Led by Dr. Pravat Surya Kar, the panel – Dr. Ajit Parulekar, Dr. Neeraj Amarnani, Dr. Vishwesh Singbal, and Dr. Shawnn Coutinho along with Dr. Kanupriya Katyal & Dr Sneha Bhat– shared honest reflections on:
·       Transitioning from corporate to academia – how “academics happened” to many of them, and why the classroom still remains their favourite place in a B-school.
·       What keeps them going – the joy of seeing concepts “click” for young, curious minds and the freedom to design one’s own learning agenda as a faculty member.

·       Teaching Gen Z – why industry experience alone is not enough; preparation, strong fundamentals and varied pedagogy (cases, simulations, role plays, exercises) are essential to earn students’ respect today.

·       The PhD / Executive FPM route – the rigour, family support and self-discipline it demands, and how GIM’s upcoming Executive FPM/PhD is structured to help working professionals make this shift without diluting academic standards.
We were delighted to see 50+ alumni join live, ask sharp questions and express interest in guest teaching, mentoring and doctoral studies.
This is just the beginning of building a stronger GIM alumni–academia bridge.
Watch out for our next announcement in this series!

Student Alumni Relations Cell (SARC) × Alumni Office Discussion on Imprints
1. Background Discussion
* It was discussed that Imprints started after 2020.
* Over time, the nature of Imprints has become more casual and informal, which was highlighted as a concern.
* The current Executive Committee (EC) made it clear that only decisions aligned with their direction will be executed.
1. Changes in College Involvement
* Goa Institute of Management, SARC, and the Alumni Office will have limited decision-making authority in certain aspects, as some requests/proposals are being directly declined by GIMAA.

* The college is not sending faculty representatives for Imprints events. This approach is expected to continue moving forward. The intent behind this is to ensure that Imprints is perceived as a more casual alumni-driven engagement rather than a formal institutional event.
1. Ownership of Imprints
* Imprints was clarified as a property of GIM Alumni Association.
* The expectation is that alumni should drive the events end-to-end.
1. SARC Travel Policy
* SARC members will not travel for general Imprints events.
* Their role will primarily remain operational and coordination-focused.
* Travel may only be considered for domain-specific events, such as:
* HR Meets
* Other specialized networking events
1. Subsidy for Recent Graduates
* It was proposed that recent passing-out batches may receive additional subsidies to help them settle in new cities.
Proposed subsidy range:
This would be a goodwill gesture for alumni who are newly relocating.
1. City Classification Changes
Previous Model:
* Flagship cities
* Non-flagship cities
New Model (From this year onwards):
Imprints can now happen across:
* Indian cities (e.g., Kochi, Ahmedabad, Pune)
* Global cities as well
Funding Discussion:
* Indian cities will definitely receive subsidies.
* For global cities, funding/subsidy may be negotiated depending on sustainability and cost optimization.
1. Stakeholder Responsibilities
It was emphasized that every stakeholder must have clearly defined responsibilities.
A. SARC Responsibilities
1. Registration management
2. Venue/on-ground logistics coordination if needed
3. Calling and promotional outreach
4. Bulk calling campaigns
5. Managing alumni outreach using data provided by the Alumni Office
* Currently ~30% pure alumni data is available
* Full data expected by end of May
1. Collecting event money/payments
2. Transferring collected funds to the Alumni Office
B. GIMAA Responsibilities
GIM Alumni Association will handle:
1. Funding support
2. Deciding event format
3. Assigning their Point of Contact (POC)
4. Venue identification through their existing local setup/network
5. Managing heavy lifting related to event setup
Exception:
* In cities where there is no GIMAA representative/member available, SARC + Alumni Office will take ownership.
* They will coordinate directly with local alumni while GIMAA provides funding support.
C. Alumni Office Responsibilities
The Alumni Office at Goa Institute of Management will manage:
1. Financial management
2. Supporting SARC with alumni database access for outreach
1. Priority Cities
Fixed Cities:
* Delhi
* Mumbai
* Bengaluru
Additional Cities:
* Hyderabad
* Kolkata
Other Potential Cities:
* Chennai
* Pune, etc (These cities may be finalized through a polling process. For these, a communication message needs to be shared with Amit Sir to ensure proper messaging is conveyed.
Suggested messaging:
Last year, we had planned events in certain cities but were unable to execute them. This year, we are actively planning these meets and encouraging registrations, etc)
9. Communication:The communication should focus on:
* Building excitement
* Driving registrations
* Ensuring clarity on upcoming city meets
1. Event Scheduling
If the main event is scheduled on a Saturday, related activities should be planned on:
* Thursday OR
* Friday (half-day)
This allows smoother coordination and execution.
Key Takeaways
* Imprints will become more alumni-driven
* Clear division of responsibilities established
* Limited institutional involvement from GIM
* Subsidy model under discussion
* Focus on improving execution and registrations
